about: Every secret this repo's commands and GitHub workflows use: its name, where it goes and how it is checked. Never a value. Read by commands/secrets.ps1.

archive.name: portal-backend.7z
archive.about: secrets -Seal packs every file and value below into this 7-Zip archive, AES-256 with its file names hidden. A copy kept in the repo at archive.local, gitignored, is what secrets -Import puts in place and -Export writes; -For looks there first. CI downloads it from SHARED_FILES_URL and opens it with SHARED_FILES_PASSWORD. Every repo in the group shares the folder and the password.

purposes.deploy-staging: server/deploy-release -Debug: install the API on the Test Server with deployment/server/deploy-admin.sh
purposes.deploy-production: server/deploy-release: install the API on production
purposes.workstation: a workstation's own setup - the API's local .env; deploys keep the server's own
purposes.settings-staging: deploy/push-env: the Test Server's secret settings, from this repo's .env - the Maintenance workflow's push-settings
purposes.settings-production: deploy/push-env -Target production: production's own secret settings, from production-settings.env

secrets.name: TOOLKIT_BITBUCKET_TOKEN
secrets.description: A Bitbucket token that can read ikaika-web/ikaika_scripts, so the runner can fetch decoupled-script.
secrets.setup: Bitbucket: ikaika_scripts > Repository settings > Access tokens > Create, with Repositories: Read. Paste the token.

secrets.name: TOOLKIT_BITBUCKET_USER
secrets.description: Only when that token is an Atlassian API token rather than an access token.
secrets.setup: Leave it unset for a repository access token (the workflow then uses x-token-auth); for an API token set it to x-bitbucket-api-token-auth.

secrets.name: BITBUCKET_REPO_TOKEN
secrets.description: A Bitbucket token on this repo: every run reads Bitbucket with it to bring GitHub up to date, and a Build release with a version bump pushes the version commit and tag with it.
secrets.setup: Bitbucket: this repo > Repository settings > Access tokens > Create, with Repositories: Read, or Read and Write to bump versions from GitHub - and the branch must not restrict pushes, since an access token cannot be given branch permissions.

secrets.name: BITBUCKET_REPO_USER
secrets.description: Only when BITBUCKET_REPO_TOKEN is an Atlassian API token rather than an access token.
secrets.setup: Leave it unset for a repository access token (the workflow then uses x-token-auth); for an API token set it to x-bitbucket-api-token-auth.

secrets.name: GH_MIRROR_TOKEN
secrets.description: A fine-grained GitHub token that can push to this repo, workflow files included, so each run can mirror Bitbucket into it.
secrets.setup: GitHub: your profile Settings > Developer settings > Fine-grained tokens > Generate; resource owner IKAIKA-OPC, only this repository (or both portal repos), Contents and Workflows: Read and write. Named GH_, not GITHUB_: GitHub refuses secret names that start with GITHUB_.

secrets.name: SHARED_FILES_URL
secrets.description: The shared folder link holding the portal repos' sealed archives, portal-backend.7z and portal-frontend.7z.
secrets.setup: Dropbox: share the folder holding the archives as 'Anyone with the link' and paste the link - a dl=0 link works, it is turned into dl=1. Never commit it.

secrets.name: SHARED_FILES_PASSWORD
secrets.description: The password the archives are sealed with, the same in both portal repos.
secrets.setup: .\script.ps1 secrets -Seal makes it on first use and keeps it for your Windows account; .\script.ps1 secrets -GitHub copies it.

secrets.name: DEPLOY_ENV_DEBUG
secrets.description: The Test Server's SSH login: Hostname, SSHUsername, SSHPASSPHRASE, and DIR - the folder deploy-admin.sh works in, apps/test-server. Also AZURE_REDIRECT_URI, the address Microsoft sign-in returns to, which the deploy writes into the API's .env.
secrets.setup: Copy .ikaika_scripts_configs/debug.env.template - the same in both portal repos - to debug.env: the project estimator's Hostname, SSHUsername and SSHPASSPHRASE, with DIR=apps/test-server as the template has it. One debug.env serves both portal repos.

secrets.name: DEPLOY_ENV_RELEASE
secrets.description: Production's SSH login, once there is a production: Hostname, SSHUsername, SSHPASSPHRASE and DIR. Also AZURE_REDIRECT_URI, the address Microsoft sign-in returns to, which the deploy writes into the API's .env.
secrets.setup: Not needed until production is set up; then copy .ikaika_scripts_configs/release.env.template - the same in both portal repos - to release.env, and use that one file in both.

secrets.name: SSH_PRIVATE_KEY
secrets.description: The SSH deploy key, ~/.ssh/project_estimator - the same Bluehost account, and the same key, the project estimator deploys with.
secrets.setup: Already on a machine that deploys the project estimator; otherwise get it from the team's shared deploy folder, or cPanel > Security > SSH Access, and save it as ~/.ssh/project_estimator.

secrets.name: APP_DOTENV
secrets.description: The API's local .env: the local databases, mail and keys a workstation runs it with. Never committed, and never deployed - the server keeps its own, which setup-env.sh and merge-env.sh manage.
secrets.setup: Run .\\script.ps1 secrets -Import to take it from the archive in the repo, or copy .env.example and fill it in.

secrets.name: PRODUCTION_SETTINGS_ENV
secrets.description: Production's own secret settings, the keys deploy/push-env sends - its Jira project and webhook secret, Cloudinary, mail relay and the rest - as KEY=value lines. Never the Test Server's: production files into the real Jira project.
secrets.setup: Copy the keys deployment/push-env.ps1 lists from .env into .ikaika_scripts_configs/production-settings.env with production's values, then .\script.ps1 secrets -Seal.
